final_message:
`BRIEFING.md` is written. Summary of what it contains and how it was produced:

**Computation** — Python `Decimal` script over the three files: each transaction converted at its `rates.csv` rate (USD 0.92, GBP 1.17), rounded to the cent *per transaction*, then summed. Percentages to one decimal.

**Key figures**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Total Q2 spend | €44,023.75 (120 transactions) |
| Average transaction | €366.86 |
| Largest transaction | €1,312.26 (hardware cables, 23 May, GBP 1,121.59) |
| May vs April | +9.8% |
| June vs May | +10.0% |
| Travel share | 27.6% |

**Category breakdown** — travel (€12,137.98 / €10,300 — **over**) and software (€9,702.03 / €8,200 — **over**); training, hardware, meals, office all under. Aggregate spend was €1,276.25 under the €45,300 budget total, so the headline masks the two overruns.

**Trends and risks flagged in the prose**: the ~10%/month compounding growth; the June travel spike (€7,065.32 — 68.5% of the quarterly travel budget in one month, with four €1,000+ ground-transport/rental transactions); recurring software spend driving an 18.3% overrun; and an anomalous pattern of 8 repeated "dock" purchases totalling €5,043.25, plus the €1.3k cable purchase as the largest single transaction.

Structure follows the spec exactly — the four `##` headings in order, the six required row labels in Key figures, and the four-column category table. No git commits were made.
